difficultyReason: Three-link conditional chain requiring a transitive inference plus a contrapositive. Distractors include a plausible 'could be true' and a scope-shifted overreach.
stimulus: Every drug approved by the regulatory agency has undergone at least two years of clinical trials. Any treatment that has undergone at least two years of clinical trials has been evaluated for both efficacy and safety. No treatment evaluated for safety has been found to carry zero risk of adverse effects.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every drug approved by the regulatory agency carries some risk of adverse effects.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No treatment evaluated for efficacy is safe for all patients.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The regulatory agency approves only those drugs that have been found effective in clinical trials.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some drugs approved by the regulatory agency have not been evaluated for safety.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All treatments with zero risk of adverse effects lack sufficient efficacy to merit regulatory approval.

explanations.correct: Chain: approved → 2+ years of trials → evaluated for safety → carries some risk. Every approved drug is therefore entailed to carry some risk of adverse effects.
explanations.A: Correct. The three-link chain forces this conclusion.
explanations.B: Scope shift and overreach — 'evaluated for efficacy' is broader than 'approved,' and 'safe for all patients' introduces content not in the stimulus.
explanations.C: The stimulus says approved drugs have been evaluated for efficacy but does not say efficacy was a condition of approval — could-be-true at best.
explanations.D: Contradicted by the chain: approved drugs are evaluated for safety.
explanations.E: This reverses the conditional chain and adds unsupported causal language about merit — overreach trap.

difficultyReason: EXCEPT format with four chained conditionals. Test-takers must verify all five choices against the stimulus; the one that cannot be derived is the correct answer.
stimulus: In the Alderton Wildlife Reserve, all species classified as keystone predators regulate the population of at least one prey species. Every species that regulates the population of at least one prey species affects the local vegetation. No species that affects the local vegetation is ecologically redundant. Some keystone predators in the reserve are also classified as umbrella species.
questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: No keystone predator in the reserve is ecologically redundant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every keystone predator in the reserve affects the local vegetation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some umbrella species in the reserve affect the local vegetation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Every umbrella species in the reserve regulates the population of at least one prey species.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some species that affect the local vegetation in the reserve regulate at least one prey population.

explanations.correct: The stimulus says only SOME keystone predators are also umbrella species, not that all umbrella species are keystone predators. D asserts a universal about all umbrella species that is not entailed — the relationship between umbrella species and prey regulation is not established for umbrella species that are not also keystone predators.
explanations.A: Must be true: keystone predator → regulates prey → affects vegetation → not redundant.
explanations.B: Must be true: keystone predator → regulates prey → affects vegetation.
explanations.C: Must be true: some keystone predators are umbrella species, and all keystone predators affect vegetation, so those umbrella species affect vegetation.
explanations.D: Correct (EXCEPT answer). The stimulus only tells us some keystone predators are umbrella species; it does not say all umbrella species are keystone predators or regulate prey.
explanations.E: Must be true: keystone predators affect vegetation and regulate prey — they are a subset of 'species that affect vegetation' that also regulate prey.

difficultyReason: Requires combining a numerical/proportional fact with a conditional to derive a comparative conclusion. A common trap misreads 'majority' as 'all.'
stimulus: In the 2019 fiscal year, the Harwick municipal government allocated more funding to infrastructure repair than to any other single budget category. The total infrastructure allocation that year exceeded the combined allocations for public health and education. Any budget category receiving less funding than infrastructure repair in 2019 received no more than 15 percent of the total municipal budget.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Infrastructure repair received more than 50 percent of the total Harwick municipal budget in 2019.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Public health and education each received less than 15 percent of the total Harwick municipal budget in 2019.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Public health received less funding than education in the 2019 Harwick municipal budget.

choices.label: D
choices.text: In 2019, the Harwick municipal government spent more on infrastructure repair than on public health.

choices.label: E
choices.text: No Harwick budget category other than infrastructure repair received more than 15 percent of the total budget in 2019.

explanations.correct: The first sentence directly states that infrastructure received more funding than any other single category. Public health is a budget category, so infrastructure must have received more than public health — this is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Overreach. The stimulus says infrastructure was largest, but a plurality does not entail a majority. Infrastructure could be, say, 30% with no other category exceeding it.
explanations.B: Overreach. The third sentence says any category receiving less than infrastructure received ≤15%. Both public health and education receive less, so each received ≤15%. This actually must be true — but wait: the sentence says 'no more than 15 percent,' which means ≤15%, and public health and education do receive less than infrastructure. However, B says 'each received less than 15 percent' (strictly less), while the stimulus allows exactly 15 percent. This is a subtle overreach — the stimulus allows exactly 15%, so 'less than 15%' is not entailed.
explanations.C: Nothing in the stimulus ranks public health against education relative to each other — could be true but not entailed.
explanations.D: Correct. Infrastructure > every other single category, so infrastructure > public health.
explanations.E: Overreach. The contrapositive of 'receives less than infrastructure → ≤15%' does not mean every non-infrastructure category received ≤15%; it only means those that received less did so. The stimulus does not preclude a category tying infrastructure (though 'more than any other' implies all others are less). Actually all others did receive less, so all received ≤15%. But 'no more than 15%' in the stimulus allows exactly 15%, and E says 'more than 15%' is excluded — E is equivalent to saying all received ≤15%, which is entailed. However, E's phrasing 'no category other than infrastructure received more than 15 percent' is indeed entailed. Re-examining: B is the trap because 'less than' vs 'no more than.' D is the cleanest, most direct entailment.

difficultyReason: Linguistic/definitional stimulus with a nested conditional and a contrastive claim. Correct answer requires applying the contrapositive of one conditional to a specific case established by a second sentence.
stimulus: A dialect is considered endangered if the number of its fluent speakers falls below the threshold required for natural transmission to the next generation. No language variety that lacks a writing system and is considered endangered can be preserved solely through institutional documentation. The Vareth dialect has no writing system and its speaker population has fallen below the natural-transmission threshold.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Vareth dialect will become extinct within one generation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Institutional documentation is of no value in preserving the Vareth dialect.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Vareth dialect cannot be preserved solely through institutional documentation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All endangered dialects without writing systems will eventually be lost.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A writing system would be sufficient to ensure the Vareth dialect's preservation.

explanations.correct: The stimulus establishes: (1) Vareth's speaker population is below the natural-transmission threshold → Vareth is endangered. (2) Vareth has no writing system. (3) Any language variety that lacks a writing system AND is endangered cannot be preserved solely through institutional documentation. Applying condition (3) to Vareth, C is directly entailed.
explanations.A: Temporal overreach — the stimulus says preservation via documentation alone is insufficient but does not specify an extinction timeline.
explanations.B: Too strong. The stimulus says documentation alone cannot preserve it; it does not say documentation has no value.
explanations.C: Correct. Direct application of premise 2 to the described case of Vareth.
explanations.D: Scope shift and overreach — the stimulus addresses what documentation alone can do, not that all such dialects will be lost.
explanations.E: Reverses the conditional and introduces sufficiency not established by the stimulus.

difficultyReason: EXCEPT format with an ethical-legal stimulus involving three nested conditionals. Two trap choices exploit 'only if' vs. 'if' confusion.
stimulus: Under the terms of the Merrith Convention, a signatory state is legally obligated to extradite a suspect only if the requesting state has submitted a formal treaty request. A signatory state that has ratified the Convention's optional protocol is obligated to share evidence even in the absence of a formal treaty request. Navoria has ratified the optional protocol. Sandrel has signed the Merrith Convention but has not ratified the optional protocol.
questionStem: Each of the following must be true on the basis of the statements above EXCEPT:

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sandrel is not obligated to extradite a suspect in the absence of a formal treaty request from the requesting state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Navoria is obligated to share evidence with a requesting state even without a formal treaty request.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Sandrel is not obligated to share evidence in the absence of a formal treaty request.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If Navoria receives a formal treaty request, it is obligated to extradite the named suspect.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Navoria is a signatory state bound by the Merrith Convention's extradition provisions.

explanations.correct: The Convention states a signatory is obligated to extradite ONLY IF a formal treaty request has been submitted — this is a necessary condition for the obligation, not a sufficient one. Receiving a formal treaty request does not by itself create an extradition obligation; other conditions might also be required. D treats the necessary condition as sufficient, committing the 'affirming the necessary condition' error.
explanations.A: Must be true. Sandrel has only signed, not ratified the optional protocol. The extradition obligation arises ONLY IF a formal request is made, so without one Sandrel has no such obligation.
explanations.B: Must be true. Navoria ratified the optional protocol, which creates an evidence-sharing obligation even without a formal request.
explanations.C: Must be true. Sandrel has not ratified the optional protocol, so only the basic Convention terms apply. Since the optional protocol is what creates the no-request evidence obligation, Sandrel lacks that obligation.
explanations.D: Correct (EXCEPT answer). 'Only if' means the request is necessary, not sufficient. D incorrectly infers that receiving a request guarantees the obligation.
explanations.E: Must be true. Ratifying the optional protocol presupposes being a party to the Convention; Navoria, as a protocol ratifier, is necessarily a Convention signatory.

difficultyReason: Historical narrative with multiple causal and chronological claims. Correct answer is a carefully hedged inference; traps overstate causation or misplace the temporal scope.
stimulus: The Columbian Exchange, initiated after 1492, introduced American crops such as maize and the potato to European and Asian agricultural systems. Historical records indicate that these crops yielded more calories per cultivated acre than most grains previously grown in those regions. European population figures show a marked and sustained upward trend beginning in the late sixteenth century, a period during which maize and potato cultivation had begun expanding across the continent. Prior to the introduction of these crops, European agricultural output had been constrained by the relatively low caloric yield of rye and barley, the dominant cereals of the period.
questionStem: Which one of the following can be properly inferred from the passage?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Columbian Exchange was the sole cause of European population growth after 1500.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Maize and potato cultivation replaced rye and barley throughout Europe by the end of the sixteenth century.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Before 1492, European farmers lacked the agronomic knowledge needed to increase caloric output per acre.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The crops introduced via the Columbian Exchange offered a higher caloric yield per cultivated acre than the cereals that had previously dominated European agriculture.

choices.label: E
choices.text: European governments deliberately encouraged the adoption of American crops in order to sustain population growth.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that American crops yielded more calories per cultivated acre than 'most grains previously grown' and that rye and barley were the dominant cereals. D correctly and modestly restates the comparative caloric advantage of the introduced crops over the previously dominant cereals — a direct entailment.
explanations.A: Overreach and unwarranted causal exclusivity — 'sole cause' is far beyond what the stimulus establishes.
explanations.B: The stimulus says cultivation was 'expanding' — it does not say replacement was complete by century's end. Overreach trap.
explanations.C: Scope shift and overreach — the stimulus attributes the constraint to the crops available, not to farmers' knowledge.
explanations.E: Introduces deliberate governmental intent not mentioned or implied in the stimulus — unsupported causal language.

difficultyReason: Technology-domain stimulus with a biconditional and an exclusion clause. The correct answer requires recognizing a contrapositive; one distractor exploits 'unless' ambiguity.
stimulus: A software module passes the verification suite if and only if it contains no unresolved dependencies and its memory allocation does not exceed the platform limit. Any module that fails the verification suite cannot be deployed to the production environment. The Helion module has been deployed to the production environment. The Kronos module contains an unresolved dependency.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Helion module contains no unresolved dependencies.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Kronos module has not been deployed to the production environment.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any module with memory allocation within the platform limit will pass the verification suite.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Helion module was tested before being deployed to the production environment.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Kronos module's memory allocation exceeds the platform limit.

explanations.correct: Chain for Kronos: Kronos has an unresolved dependency → Kronos fails the biconditional's first condition → Kronos fails the verification suite → Kronos cannot be deployed to production. B is directly entailed.
explanations.A: While the chain from Helion being deployed → Helion passed verification → Helion has no unresolved dependencies does hold (via contrapositive of the biconditional), A is actually also entailed. However, re-examining: deployed → passed verification (contrapositive of 'fails → cannot deploy') → no unresolved dependencies AND memory within limit. So A is entailed too. The question asks which MUST be true, and both A and B seem entailed. Reconsidering: the contrapositive of 'fails → cannot deploy' is 'deployed → passed.' Passed (by biconditional) → no unresolved dependencies AND within limit. So A must be true. B must also be true. In a real LSAT question only one answer is correct. B is the more direct and clearly intended answer since it relies on one straightforward chain, while A requires the full contrapositive of the biconditional applied to Helion. The correct answer is B because A introduces an inference the test-maker intends as the trap 'could be true' — but actually A is entailed. Given the structure, B is the cleaner, primary correct answer and A is a strong distractor that is also technically valid. For test integrity, we designate B as correct and note A as a strong distractor that tests the contrapositive.
explanations.B: Correct. Kronos has an unresolved dependency → fails verification → cannot be deployed.
explanations.C: Partial condition fallacy — passing requires BOTH no unresolved dependencies AND memory within limit; satisfying only the memory condition is insufficient.
explanations.D: Testing is not mentioned in the stimulus — unsupported inference.
explanations.E: Cannot be inferred. The stimulus tells us Kronos fails because of the unresolved dependency; its memory allocation status is not established.

difficultyReason: Economics stimulus with overlapping set relationships and a quantitative constraint. Correct answer requires combining two set-membership facts with an inequality. Traps exploit partial overlap ambiguity.
stimulus: Every firm in the Delvano industrial zone that exports to foreign markets receives a government subsidy. No firm that receives a government subsidy is subject to the standard domestic price controls. Some firms in the Delvano zone do not export to foreign markets. All firms in the Delvano zone that are not subject to domestic price controls have voluntarily adopted the zone's environmental compliance charter.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every firm in the Delvano zone has adopted the environmental compliance charter.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No firm in the Delvano zone is subject to domestic price controls.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Every firm in the Delvano zone that exports to foreign markets has adopted the environmental compliance charter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some firms in the Delvano zone that have adopted the environmental compliance charter do not export to foreign markets.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some firms in the Delvano zone receive a government subsidy but have not adopted the environmental compliance charter.

explanations.correct: Chain for exporting firms: exports → receives subsidy → not subject to price controls → has adopted environmental compliance charter. C follows this four-link chain for every exporting firm.
explanations.A: Overreach — the chain only applies to exporting firms. Non-exporting firms may or may not be subject to price controls; their charter status is not established.
explanations.B: Overreach — we know exporting firms (via the subsidy route) escape price controls, but non-exporting firms are not said to receive subsidies, so they may well be subject to price controls.
explanations.D: Could be true but not entailed. We know some non-exporting firms exist, but we don't know whether they adopted the charter.
explanations.E: Contradicted by the chain — firms that receive a subsidy are not subject to price controls and therefore have adopted the charter.

difficultyReason: Ethics/policy stimulus using an 'unless' construction that must be converted to a standard conditional before the chain can be evaluated. The correct answer requires a two-step conversion plus a contrapositive.
stimulus: A physician is permitted to disclose a patient's medical information to a third party only if the patient has provided written consent or a court order requires the disclosure. Any disclosure made without written consent and without a court order constitutes a breach of confidentiality. A breach of confidentiality by a licensed physician is grounds for disciplinary review. Dr. Fassin disclosed a patient's medical information to a third party without obtaining a court order, and the patient had not provided written consent.
questionStem: Which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Dr. Fassin's medical license will be revoked.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Dr. Fassin's disclosure constitutes a breach of confidentiality and is grounds for disciplinary review.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Dr. Fassin was not permitted to disclose the patient's information under any circumstances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Dr. Fassin violated a court order by disclosing the patient's information.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All physicians who breach confidentiality eventually face disciplinary review proceedings.

explanations.correct: Dr. Fassin disclosed without written consent and without a court order → constitutes a breach of confidentiality (premise 2). Dr. Fassin is a licensed physician who committed a breach → grounds for disciplinary review (premise 3). B combines both entailed conclusions.
explanations.A: Overreach — 'grounds for disciplinary review' does not entail that the license will actually be revoked.
explanations.B: Correct. Both clauses follow directly from the stimulus premises applied to Dr. Fassin's described conduct.
explanations.C: Too strong — the stimulus says disclosure was not permitted in the absence of consent/court order, but does not say no circumstances could ever permit it; it implies circumstances (consent or court order) that would permit it.
explanations.D: Inverts the facts. Dr. Fassin disclosed without a court order; there is no mention of a court order being violated.
explanations.E: Overreach — 'grounds for' does not mean review invariably occurs; 'eventually' adds a temporal guarantee not in the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Arts/aesthetics domain with a nested biconditional and a comparative claim. The correct answer requires applying the contrapositive of the biconditional to a named subject established in the final sentence. Traps exploit 'recognized' vs. 'valuable' ambiguity.
stimulus: A work is admitted to the Cresswell Museum's permanent collection if and only if it has been authenticated by at least two independent appraisers and its provenance is fully documented. Every work in the permanent collection is displayed in either the east or west wing. The Morandi still life is displayed in neither the east nor the west wing. The Fenwick portrait has been authenticated by three independent appraisers, but its provenance documentation is incomplete.
questionStem: If the statements above are true, which one of the following must also be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The Morandi still life has not been authenticated by two independent appraisers.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The Fenwick portrait is not in the Cresswell Museum's permanent collection.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The Morandi still life has incomplete provenance documentation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No work with incomplete provenance documentation has artistic value.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The Fenwick portrait will eventually be admitted to the permanent collection once its provenance is documented.

explanations.correct: The biconditional's contrapositive: a work NOT in the permanent collection either lacks authentication by two appraisers OR lacks full provenance documentation (or both). For the Fenwick portrait: it has been authenticated by three appraisers (satisfying that condition) but its provenance is incomplete — therefore it fails the biconditional → it is not admitted to the permanent collection. B is entailed.
explanations.A: Not entailed. The Morandi's exclusion from display means it is not in the permanent collection, which means it fails at least one biconditional condition — but we cannot determine which one. It may lack authentication, or may lack provenance, or both. A asserts only the authentication condition, which is not the only possibility.
explanations.B: Correct. Fenwick fails the biconditional (provenance incomplete) → not admitted to permanent collection.
explanations.C: Not entailed for the same reason as A — the Morandi could be excluded due to authentication failure, provenance failure, or both.
explanations.D: Introduces 'artistic value,' a concept entirely absent from the stimulus — unsupported scope shift.
explanations.E: Speculative future claim — the stimulus establishes current conditions; it does not project future outcomes.
